survived_hypothesis.candidate_label: Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS A)
survived_hypothesis.statement: If Alzheimer's Disease and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS A) may rely on the same representation-carrying bottleneck rather than only sharing a task family, then when training on Alzheimer's Disease and evaluating on Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS A) versus training on the same anchor and evaluating on task-mismatched controls is manipulated relative to the task-mismatched or label-shuffled transfer baseline, cross-condition decoding accuracy anchored on Alzheimer's Disease should remain above the transfer baseline only when the shared bottleneck is present.
survived_hypothesis.mechanism: Alzheimer's Disease and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS A) may rely on the same representation-carrying bottleneck rather than only sharing a task family.
survived_hypothesis.independent_variable: training on Alzheimer's Disease and evaluating on Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS A) versus training on the same anchor and evaluating on task-mismatched controls
survived_hypothesis.dependent_variable: cross-condition decoding accuracy anchored on Alzheimer's Disease
survived_hypothesis.control_condition: the task-mismatched or label-shuffled transfer baseline
survived_hypothesis.minimal_test: Train on Alzheimer's Disease, test on Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS A), and compare transfer accuracy against a label-shuffled or task-mismatched baseline.
survived_hypothesis.falsifier: Reject this transfer hypothesis if cross-condition performance between Alzheimer's Disease and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS A) stays at control levels.
